$comment: ADR-0017 §6's merge table, one entry per property of Evaluated_Requirement, in the ADR's own order. It is the checkable link between the ADR prose and the two roll-up implementations: shared/go/rollup_test.go and shared/typescript/rollup.test.ts both assert that this file's field set is exactly the schema's Evaluated_Requirement property set, so a new schema field cannot land without a recorded merge rule, and both read the same rule names, so the languages cannot drift. adrRule quotes the ADR row (markdown emphasis stripped); a reviewer checks the implementation by reading dev-docs/adr-0017-raw-source-artifact-carriage-and-requirement-rollup.md §6 beside this file.

rules.mergeKey: The field entries are grouped by. Identical across a group by construction.
rules.concat: Concatenate the members' values in source order.
rules.union: Union the members' values, first-seen order preserved. De-duplication is about what the MERGE adds: a later member's value already present is not appended. A member's own repeated values are left exactly as the converter emitted them — the output is not re-written into a set, because silently dropping a duplicate the converter chose to emit is the data loss this rule's whole-member identity was picked to avoid. The consequence is that de-duplication is asymmetric by design, not by oversight.
rules.tagsPerKey: Per tag key: a key both members carry as an array unions; every other key first-wins; a key only a later member carries is added. ONE EXCEPTION: the unrated-severity marker (severity_rating: unrated) is derived, not a tag — it survives only if EVERY member carried it, because it asserts the severity was defaulted rather than rated.
rules.worstWins: The worst value across the members wins, whatever the member order. Absent loses to present.
rules.firstWins: The first member's value wins — present or absent. A later member contributes nothing.
rules.derived: Not merged. Recomputed after merging from the merged results and overrides, so the helper drops the pre-merge values rather than carrying the first member's.

fields.note: The marker tag severity_rating=unrated is computed during the merge as an AND across the members, not merged as a scalar key. Merged as a tag it is wrong both ways: added from a later member it labels a rated requirement unrated; kept from the first member it claims no rating beside a genuine worst-wins severity. Unlike the derived fields, the caller cannot recompute it — after merging nothing distinguishes a rated severity from one defaulted to 0.5.
